fx_note: AUD at 112.37 JPY/AUD (2026-08-16). AUD figures are CALCULATION.

critical_definitions.per_person_per_night: Japanese lodges and pensions overwhelmingly price PER PERSON PER NIGHT, often including breakfast or half board. This is NOT comparable with Western whole-property nightly rates without dividing by capacity.
critical_definitions.whole_property: Rate for exclusive use of the entire property regardless of occupancy.
critical_definitions.derived_per_guest: whole_property rate divided by stated maximum capacity. A CALCULATION, and an upper bound on realised per-guest revenue because properties rarely sell at full capacity.
critical_definitions.inclusions_warning: Rates including meals are NOT comparable with self-catering rates. Half-board ryokan rates can be 2-4x business hotel rates largely because of food. Each observation below records inclusions.

national_context.source: Japanese hotel-industry analysis citing JTA data. Direct fetch of the publisher returned HTTP 403; figures taken from the search index.
national_context.caveat: These are PER ROOM rates for hotels/ryokan across all of Japan, dominated by urban and high-end properties. They are context, NOT a benchmark for a self-catering ski lodge.

hakuba.evidence_quality: STRONG - a complete published rate card with defined seasons

season_definition.IMPLICATION: The operator's own high season is only 76 days. Earlier modelling assumed a 100-140 night sellable core season. If 76 days is representative, the revenue base is materially narrower than assumed and the minpaku 180-night cap is even less binding.

source.name: Mojo Lodge Hakuba published rate card

hakuba.inclusions: Full daily breakfast, airport/valley transfer, morning ski shuttle, wifi, 10% consumption tax
hakuba.minimum_stay: 7 nights in peak season; 1-2 night stays incur a 4,000 JPY surcharge
hakuba.long_stay_discounts: 5-30% for 10+ nights, scaling to 30% for 60+ nights

KEY_FINDING_bathroom_premium.comparison: Twin/Queen double with PRIVATE bathroom 19,000 JPY vs Twin/Double double with SHARED bathroom 15,500 JPY, both high season
KEY_FINDING_bathroom_premium.significance: Quantifies the bathroom constraint identified in the property analysis. A private bathroom commands roughly a 23% rate premium in the same lodge, which is the return on the most expensive renovation category in a snow-country building.

myoko.evidence_quality: GOOD - nine independent data points, no single published rate card

observations.note: Highest per-guest rate observed in Myoko
Coastal Joetsu-Myoko, not the ski village - a location discount comparator
Ensuite per room, heated flooring, described as luxury
Twin room. Also cited: 10th night free on 10-night stays

myoko.minimum_stay_evidence: Yuki Lodge (Ikenotaira): 5 nights minimum in peak season (pre-Christmas to early March)

niseko_kutchan.evidence_quality: MEDIUM - a stated market range plus two points; extreme dispersion
niseko_kutchan.range_note: A 13x spread. Niseko is not one rate market - it spans budget cabins to ultra-luxury villas, and a market-level average would be meaningless.
niseko_kutchan.booking_behaviour: January and February sell out; bookings typically open in March for the following winter.

nozawa_onsen.evidence_quality: WEAK - capacity data good, rate data poor. Operators use dynamic pricing behind booking engines.

observations.note: Rates dynamic, not published. 25% non-refundable deposit, 75% balance 100 days before arrival.

nozawa_onsen.gap: No published seasonal rate card obtained. Two operator sites returned HTTP 403.

KEY_FINDING.statement: Yuzawa whole-rental rates start around 4,000 JPY per guest per night, roughly a QUARTER of Hakuba's high-season per-person rate of 15,500 JPY.
KEY_FINDING.significance: Yuzawa's depressed property prices are matched by depressed room rates. The two are consistent, which supports the value-trap reading: the asset is cheap because what it earns is cheap, not because the market has mispriced it.

madarao_iiyama.note: Madarao Kogen Hotel identified but rates only via booking engines.

benchmark_bands_per_guest_per_night._method: Derived from whole-property rates divided by stated capacity, and from published per-person rates. An UPPER BOUND on realised revenue per guest, because properties rarely sell at full capacity and shoulder rates are lower.

niseko_winter.note: Range is genuinely this wide; a central figure is not meaningful

cross_market_finding.statement: On per-guest-per-night rates, Hakuba high season (~15,500 central) is roughly 1.5x Myoko (~10,500) and roughly 1.8x Yuzawa (~8,780), with Yuzawa's floor at a quarter of Hakuba's central rate.
cross_market_finding.significance: Rate differentials are much SMALLER than land price differentials. Kutchan land is 6.1x Myoko's, but Niseko's budget-end per-guest rates (8,625) are close to Myoko's (10,500). This means cheaper markets are not proportionally less productive per guest - which is the strongest quantitative argument yet for the affordability thesis, and it cuts against the land-price-led ranking.

data_gaps: No occupancy data pairs with these rates - rates alone do not give revenue
Five of ten requested markets have no rate evidence at all
No systematic capacity-band comparison (6/8/10/12/16/20+) within a single market
Summer and autumn rates almost entirely absent
Most operators use dynamic pricing behind booking engines; published rate cards are the exception
